_comment: THE ONE ENVIRONMENT REGISTRY. Every environment variable this repository reads
or supplies, in three sections held by ONE gate, check:ci-env-registry
(`.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/env_registry.py`); read that module's docstring and
the three section modules it names before editing this file, because every
rule below is enforced there and none of it is advisory.
`shards` (with `shard_definitions`, `tombstone_proof_sites`, `collisions`,
`notes`): WHO SUPPLIES THE VALUE and WHO MAY READ IT (env_manifest.py).
`python_reads`: every `module:NAME` read of a tracked Python module, derived
from the AST and shrink-only (python_env_registry.py).
`worklist`: every WORKLIST_* name with its kind, class and pinned default
spellings (worklist_env_registry.py).
THERE IS NO COUNT IN THIS FILE, ANYWHERE, ON PURPOSE. The plan box that asked for
it quoted 1,014 names; the box's own design note re-measured 745, then 721, then
777, depending on whether one developer's `.env.pre-rename.bak` happened to be on
disk. Every number the gate prints is derived on the run that prints it. If you
are about to write a total into a comment here, do not: it will be wrong within
the week and it will be believed.
HOW TO ADD A NAME. One command, which the UNCLASSIFIED finding also names:
`npm run env:register -- <module> <NAME> --class <shard>`. It writes the name's
one authored home (a shard list, or for a WORKLIST_* name its entry under
`worklist`), re-renders the WORKLIST_* members of the shard lists from that
section, records a Python read under `python_reads` with a typed `--allow-new`,
regenerates the docs and runs the gate. It never commits. There is deliberately
no blanket reseed for the shards: that is how a fresh violation gets absorbed
alongside a legitimate drain. The verb is typed per name, so it reseeds nothing.
THE WORKLIST_* MEMBERS ARE GENERATED OUTPUT. Their shard is the `worklist`
section's `class`, and a WORKLIST_* name placed by hand in any other shard is a
finding.
HOW TO REMOVE ONE. Do not, unless the tree genuinely stopped reading it -- in
which case the gate has ALREADY told you, as STALE. A live-shard entry that no
reader finds is a red, not a tidy-up: that is the arm that keeps the manifest
shrinking rather than accumulating names nobody uses.

shard_definitions.secret: Supplied by the Bitwarden vault (.ci/config/bws-secret-map.json) or by a GitHub Actions secret, and readable only by the job or runtime that needs it. VAULT MEMBERSHIP DECIDES, not the shape of the name: ACCOUNT_ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY and STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY are public values and still belong here, because the question this shard answers is who supplies the value, and the answer for both is the vault. No value of any secret is recorded anywhere in this file or read by the gate; names only.
shard_definitions.ci-runner: Supplied by the GitHub Actions runner (GITHUB_*, RUNNER_*, CI) or by this repository's own CI orchestration: a workflow `env:` block, a job output (RESULT_*), a dispatch input, the watchdog, the autopilot. Read only inside CI; setting one on a developer machine does nothing.
shard_definitions.gate-seam: Supplied by a gate's own control or test so the gate can be pointed at a FIXTURE instead of the real tree, or so a threshold can be moved for one run. Read by exactly one gate. These are the names most often mistaken for configuration, and REDIACC_CI_ROOT is the canonical one -- `.ci/rediacc_ci/paths.py` declares it as the SINGLE such override for the whole package, replacing eight per-gate spellings.
shard_definitions.toolchain: A version pin, a checksum, or the path to a tool binary. Supplied by `.devcontainer/toolchain.env` or by whatever provisioned the host. This shard is what `check:ci-toolchain-pins` and the devcontainer image agree about.
shard_definitions.well-known: A fact the registry `.ci/config/well-known.env` declares: an origin, bucket, repository slug, image registry, owned path, address or third-party API base. Supplied by that file (read by bash through its projection `.ci/config/well-known.generated.sh`, which `.ci/config/constants.sh` sources; appended to `$GITHUB_ENV` by the 'Load well-known' step), never by the operator, so setting one on a machine overrides nothing the Python and TypeScript readers see. The WK_ prefix separates a fact from a knob such as RELEASES_BASE_URL, which is an override a developer may point elsewhere.
shard_definitions.machine-local: Supplied by the developer's operating system, shell or session. This repository only ever READS these; nothing here sets them, and nothing here may require them to be set.
shard_definitions.product-runtime: Read by SHIPPED code at run time -- the rdc CLI on a user's machine, the account worker, the marketing site. A change to one of these is a change to the product's interface, and `docs/environment-variables.md` is the user-facing reference for the CLI subset.
shard_definitions.harness: Supplied by a local test, development or agent harness: the e2e suite, the tutorial recorder, the breakpoint lab, the VM lab, the Claude hooks. Not shipped, not CI-supplied, not a gate seam.
shard_definitions.tombstone: Retired. The name must not appear in the derived corpus at all. Every entry has a replacement in `docs/environment-variables.md`; the gate fails if one comes back. A read that exists only to PROVE the name is dead is registered under `tombstone_proof_sites` by exact (path, name) pair.

_tombstone_proof_sites_comment: A file whose job is to NAME dead variables necessarily mentions them, and left in
the corpus it resurrects them into `sources` -- breaking the tombstone clause by
existing. The suppression is per (path, NAME) PAIR and never per file, and it is
liveness-checked in both directions: the pair must still be found by a reader at
that path (a dangling entry fails, so the list can only shrink), and the name must
be in the tombstone shard (so the mechanism cannot hide a live variable). Both are
The second entry is account-client.test.ts:164, which SETS X25519_PUBLIC_KEY and
asserts the config value wins anyway. That is a proof of death, not a read.

collisions.name: DEBUG
why: DEBUG is a CLI tombstone (docs/environment-variables.md:107 replaces it with REDIACC_DEBUG scopes) and, separately, the harness's own `DEBUG=true` switch (create_e2e_env.py, .ci/rediacc_ci/log.py, breakpoint-common.sh). The e2e suite's example env file that also set it is deleted (2026-09-24). Two variables that share a spelling, so a repo-wide ban would be false and it is NOT in the tombstone shard.

THE AUTHORITY IS THE DOC AND NOT THE TEST, and that is a finding rather than a preference: packages/cli/src/__tests__/env-tombstones.test.ts bans fourteen retired names and DEBUG is not one of them, so nothing in code enforces the documented deletion. This entry pointed at the test until a plant on the real tree showed the check passing for the wrong reason -- the match was a plain substring and REDIACC_DAEMON_DEBUG contains DEBUG. Both the matcher and the claim were wrong; both are fixed here.

notes.RDC_BENCH: Retired: bench is an ordinary named config (`./rdc.sh --config eu-bench`), and docs/environment-variables.md lists the name as deleted. This note once recorded the price of excluding bash ${VAR} from the corpus (.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/env_manifest.py): two shell files, .ci/lib/local-common.sh and .ci/scripts/infra/build-renet.sh, still branched on the name while three documents called it deleted, and this gate could not see them. Both files are gone (re-checked 2026-10-30), so no reader is left.
notes.REDIACC_ENVIRONMENT: Dead as a name the CLI READS. It still travels as a REMOTE renet environment value, built as a string literal in services/executor/renet-command.ts, which is none of the five source kinds and so does not collide.
notes.REDIACC_CI_ROOT: The single fixture-pointing override for the whole rediacc_ci package, declared once at .ci/rediacc_ci/paths.py:70 as ROOT_ENV. It is in this manifest only because the os-environ reader parses instead of grepping: `os.environ.get(ROOT_ENV)` is invisible to a regex over the call site, and 54 other gate seams were invisible with it.
notes.X: A PLACEHOLDER, not a variable. `process.env.X` appears inside a fixture string in scripts/gates/check-gate-cwd-independence.ts:169, which builds a synthetic gate to test its own matcher. It is classified gate-seam because that is literally what it is: a seam in a gate's own fixture. The Python reader no longer produces this class of entry (it parses), but no TypeScript parser is available to a Python gate.
notes.SOME_ROOT: The same case as X: a placeholder in the fixtures of scripts/gates/check-gate-cwd-independence.ts and in the prose of scripts/lib/repo-root.ts:15.
notes.STATE_isPost: GitHub Actions' own state channel, written by @actions/core in .github/actions/profiler/index.js. The lowercase tail is theirs, not a typo, and it is why the yaml-key matcher permits a trailing lowercase character.

python_reads.note: SHRINK-ONLY, AND GENERATED -- do not hand-edit except to re-key a moved module. Every `<module>: [NAME, ...]` here is one environment variable a tracked Python module reads, derived from the AST by python_env_registry.py. A `*` prefix means the name is not a literal at the call site and the EXPRESSION is recorded instead. The gate asserts SET EQUALITY with the tree in both directions: a read missing from here reds, and so does an entry nothing reads. Drain it with `--write-baseline`, which refuses any reseed that would ADD a pair even when the total shrinks. A genuinely new read must be typed: `--write-baseline --allow-new <module>:<NAME>`.

$why: Every WORKLIST_* environment name this repository reads, in one place, so that a name nobody reads and a read nobody registered are both findings.

THE DEFECT: a typo'd name reads as UNSET. For a flag that defaults to `on` -- WORKLIST_FOCUS until 2026-10-14 (removed by agent/plans/PLAN-stop-hook-effort.md), and until 2026-10-04 WORKLIST_AGENT_HINT, WORKLIST_AGENT_PUSHBACK and WORKLIST_CADENCE, which moved to agent/plans/QUEUE.md (WORKLIST_CADENCE came back on 2026-11-21 as an on|off test seam only, beside WORKLIST_JUDGE) -- that is the FAIL-OPEN direction: the author believes they switched something off and it is still running. Nothing in the tree said so before 2026-09-09.

Measured 2026-09-09 against the bash corpus that has since been ported to pytest: 133 live names across 60 tracked files at 183 read sites. The plan box said 134, which is the GREP answer; one of those, WORKLIST_EMAIL, appeared only in a comment describing a name that no longer existed, which is why this scanner counts READS rather than greps.

Enforced by check:ci-env-registry (the `worklist` section), both directions. The name set and each name's default spellings are DERIVED from the code by the gate and pinned here, so this file cannot drift into being a description of what somebody once intended. `kind`, `class` and `why` are the authored fields, and the gate checks each against the derived shape or its allowed set.

`class` (harness or gate-seam) is the field the `shards` section is rendered from: every WORKLIST_* member of its shard lists is generated from this section, which makes this section the one authored home of a WORKLIST_* name. `foreign_reads` holds the names read only where this scan cannot look (a TypeScript gate), each with its reader and a reason, and the gate proves the reader still names it. Register a name with `npm run env:register -- <module> <NAME> --class <c> --kind <k> --default <spelling>... [--why <w>]`, which writes this section, re-renders the shards and runs check:ci-env-registry.

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_roster.py.why: the parallel-writer roster's 20-minute status ping is the operator's (2026-09-24, 'no escape hatches'; there is no writer limit since agent/plans/PLAN-unlimited-writers.md), so no variable may retune it, or hide a live writer from supervision, and a registered knob would be exactly the hatch that was ruled out

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_standdown.py.why: the stand-down keep-lists (the concurrency-saturated wait, the PR loop and the landing tree) decide which checks still block while the session is told to wait; a variable that retuned a list or the PR-read cache would be exactly the escape hatch the roster rules out

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_floor.py.why: the Stop hook's FLOOR, the checks that block at every effort level (agent/plans/PLAN-stop-hook-effort.md); a variable that shrank it would be the off switch the effort dial replaced, so the set is a literal here and .claude/config/effort.json may only mark its keys `floor`

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_planconc.py.why: plan priority order and the plan-concurrency rules (the mutex and the Owns overlap, operator 2026-09-25 section X); a variable that retuned what counts as an overlap, or which lease counts as live, would be an escape hatch around the pre-agent guard and the roster that read it

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_planorder.py.why: the one plan order and concurrency hold every next-item picker reads (queue-slot, the guide, the open list, the backlog nomination, the queue lease beside a free slot); a variable that decided which item is held or which plan ranks first would be an escape hatch around the pre-agent guard and the roster

.claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_plan_.why: the PreToolUse half of plan concurrency: it refuses a writer spawn that breaks a live exclusive plan or claims files a live plan owns, and an environment read here would let a spawn bypass it

.claude/hooks/stop/wl_gh.py.why: the Stop hook's one gh layer (agent/plans/PLAN-ci-consolidation.md Part C): the transient-retry bound of two attempts and one 2 s pause (PLAN-gh-retry G13) and the per-spawn timeout decide how much of every stop's budget a slow or failing GitHub may spend, so no variable may stretch them

exclusions.agent/: invariant 7: agent/ is live gated state (.claude/hooks/stop/wl_store.py:274), not source. It is full of plans and briefs that NAME these variables in prose, and admitting it would register every name any plan ever discussed. Declared here rather than hardcoded in the gate so the reason travels with the exclusion.
exclusions.docs/: prose about the program, not the program. Same argument as agent/: a documented name is not a read, and a gate that treats it as one can never report a name as dead.

kinds.flag: a toggle. A typo reads as the default, which for a flag defaulting to `on` is FAIL-OPEN. `why` is REQUIRED, and every default must be one of on, off, 1, 0 or empty.
kinds.tuning: a numeric threshold, limit, count or timeout. A typo yields the default, which is fail-safe, so no `why` is required. Every default must parse as a number.
kinds.path: a directory or file location. Named `*_DIR`/`*_ROOT`, or a default containing a path separator.
kinds.handle: an identity supplied by the harness or the environment: a session id, a pid, a branch, a ref. Unset is the normal state and means `work it out`, so a typo turns a capability off silently. `why` is REQUIRED.
kinds.corpus: a pattern, list or model id that selects WHAT the program looks at or uses. Narrowing one does not make a check stricter, it makes it see less, which is the vacuity direction. `why` is REQUIRED, and this kind is deliberately the residual so that the residual cannot become a dumping ground.

WORKLIST_AGENT_BRANCH.why: The branch the worklist attributes work to, overriding the `git symbolic-ref` read in wl_core.py:573. A handle rather than a flag: unset is the normal state and means `ask git`. It is also the most-assigned name in the test corpus, which is why a typo here surfaces as a test that quietly reads the real branch.

WORKLIST_CADENCE.why: test seam only, the twin of WORKLIST_JUDGE: the cadence is decided by the effort level's bundle (the QUEUE.md fence takes effort alone, agent/plans/PLAN-simple-two-tree-loop.md B5), and env on or off overrides it (wl_checks.cadence_on) so the fixtures run with it off. Any other value is ignored.

WORKLIST_CI_RETRY_PATTERNS.why: The comma-separated job-name patterns wl_ci.py:176 will auto-retry. A corpus, not a knob: adding a pattern widens what the hook is willing to re-run on the operator's behalf, so the value is a policy decision and the default is four named job families.

WORKLIST_HARNESS_PID.why: The harness pid, overriding the ancestor walk in wl_liveness.py:172, for tests and for setups where the walk cannot see the harness. Read with `.isdigit()`, so a typo and a non-numeric value are indistinguishable from unset and both fall back to the walk.

WORKLIST_JUDGE.why: test seam only: standing on/off is agent/plans/QUEUE.md `judge:`, and env `on` or `off` overrides it (wl_judge.disabled). Any other value is ignored, so a misspelled value falls back to QUEUE.md rather than disabling a paid call.

WORKLIST_LKG_CHILD.why: The last-known-good recursion guard (wl_lkg.py, agent/plans/PLAN-stop-hook-continuity.md P2.5), set only by worklist.py on the snapshot child it spawns after a live-tree crash. Unset is the normal state. A misspelled read would read as unset inside the child, so a crashing snapshot would try to fall back again; the child's own crash then emits the ordinary crash block, which is the fail-closed direction.

WORKLIST_PROFILE.why: `off` disables the tier-0 resource profiler (wl_resprofile.py:197 and :369). Compared with `== "off"` in both places, so every other spelling leaves profiling on. Classed as a corpus rather than a flag because the bash side reads it with a different default spelling, which is itself worth seeing in this table.

WORKLIST_PROGRAM_SURFACE.why: The space-separated tree list wl_checks.py:70 treats as `the program`, split() into three roots. A corpus and not a path: it is one string holding several bare directory NAMES with no separator in any of them, and narrowing it does not make any check stricter, it makes the check see less of the program. The gate caught this entry classed as a path on its first run against the real tree, which is the shape rule doing its job.

WORKLIST_PUBLISH_REF.why: The ref a PR is published on, wl_ci.py:42 and :77. Empty means the session has not opted in and pays nothing; when it IS set and the lookup fails, that is reported as a hook-side inability rather than passing quietly. A typo therefore silently opts the session out.

WORKLIST_READ_MEMO.why: `off` turns the per-read store memo off (wl_core.py:1136); compared with != 'off', so a typo leaves the memo on, which is the fail-open direction

WORKLIST_SCHED_RED_TTL_S.why: How long wl_schedred's shared scheduled-run cache stays fresh, wl_schedred.py:32. Fifteen minutes keeps a GitHub read to about four an hour across every session while a red still surfaces within one stop of the cache expiring.

WORKLIST_SESSION_ID.why: The session identity, tried before CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in wl_core.py:313. Returns "" for CANNOT VERIFY, and the honest response to that is to say nothing rather than accuse, so a typo turns identity checking off without a word.

WORKLIST_SOURCE_OVERRIDE_FILE.why: GATE-SEAM, test-only: `rel/path:override/file`, read by check:ci-worklist-env-registry's own scan_corpus() to substitute one tracked source file's CONTENT with a tmp copy during the plant tests, so test_a_typo_in_a_real_source_file_reds never writes the real tracked file it names. Unset means no substitution: the real corpus is scanned unchanged.

WORKLIST_EPICS_LEDGER.why: read only by a TypeScript gate, as the seam that points its ledger reader at a /tmp fixture. This registry's scan reads Python and bash, so `names` cannot hold it without reporting it DEAD; it lives here so its class still renders into env-manifest, and the gate proves the reader still names it
